1	title: Fix possible SIGSEGV for web disks when file does not exists
2	category: bugfix
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Operators using web-backed disks may probe for files that are missing, and they expect a normal "not found" answer rather than an exception caused by walking past the end of the in-memory file list. Today a missing path can trigger a segmentation-fault-class failure instead of a clean absence check.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  File-existence checks for web disks should return `false` when the requested path is not present, even when the lower-bound lookup lands at the end of the available file list. Missing remote files must be handled as an expected condition, not as a low-level failure in metadata traversal.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  A lookup for a non-existent web-disk path safely reports that the file is absent, while existing-prefix checks continue to work as before and no out-of-bounds iterator access is triggered by the missing-path case.
16

---
sidebar_position: 59
sidebar_label: Named collections
---

# Named collections

Named collections provide a way to store collections of key-value pairs to be
used to configure integrations with external sources. You can use named
collections with dictionaries, table functions, table engines, and models.
The entries in a named collection are set in the server configuration file, in
the section `named_collections`. Each collection has a name, and the entries
in each collection are key-value pairs, where the value can be a string or a
number.

Named collections can be configured with DDL statements or with configuration
files, and are applied when ClickHouse starts. They can be used to configure
integrations with external sources.

## Storing named collections with DDL statements

### Permissions for managing named collections with DDL

To manage named collections with DDL statements a user must have the
`named_collection_control` privilege. The privilege can be granted with:

```sql
GRANT named_collection_control ON *.* TO user;
```

### CREATE NAMED COLLECTION

```sql
CREATE NAMED COLLECTION [IF NOT EXISTS] name [ON CLUSTER cluster]
AS
    key_1 = 'value',
    key_2 = 123
```

**Example**

```sql
CREATE NAMED COLLECTION s3_config AS
    access_key_id = 'AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE',
    secret_access_key = 'wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY',
    url = 'https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/your-bucket/';
```

### ALTER NAMED COLLECTION

```sql
ALTER NAMED COLLECTION [IF EXISTS] name [ON CLUSTER cluster]
[SET key_1 = 'value', key_2 = 123]
[DELETE key_3, key_4]
```

**Example**

```sql
ALTER NAMED COLLECTION s3_config
SET url = 'https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/your-bucket/'
DELETE access_key_id, secret_access_key;
```

### DROP NAMED COLLECTION

```sql
DROP NAMED COLLECTION [IF EXISTS] name [ON CLUSTER cluster]
```

**Example**

```sql
DROP NAMED COLLECTION s3_config;
```

## Storing named collections in the server configuration file

**Example of the configuration file**

```xml
<clickhouse>
     <named_collections>
        <s3_config>
            <access_key_id>ABC123</access_key_id>
            <secret_access_key>abc123</secret_access_key>
            <url>https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/your-bucket/</url>
        </s3_config>
     </named_collections>
</clickhouse>
```

**Usage example**

Both of the following examples use the same named collection `s3_config`:

```sql
INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3(s3_config, filename = 'test_file.tsv.gz', format = 'TSV')
SELECT * FROM source_table;

SELECT * FROM s3(s3_config, filename = 'test_function_data.csv', format = 'CSV');
```

### Example of a named collection for connecting to a ClickHouse database

```xml
<clickhouse>
    <named_collections>
        <remote1>
            <host>remote_host</host>
            <port>9000</port>
            <database>db1</database>
            <user>foo</user>
            <password>[password]</password>
        </remote1>
    </named_collections>
</clickhouse>
```

**Usage example**

```sql
SELECT * FROM remote(remote1, db1, table1);
SELECT * FROM remoteSecure(remote1, db1, table1);
SELECT * FROM cluster(cluster1, db1, table1);
```

+

+* Changes how settings using `seconds` as type are parsed to support floating point values (for example: `max_execution_time=0.5`). Infinity or NaN values will throw an exception. [#37187](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/37187) ([Raúl Marín](https://github.com/Algunenano)).

+* Added `SYSTEM UNFREEZE` query that deletes the whole backup regardless if the corresponding table is deleted or not. [#36424](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/36424) ([Vadim Volodin](https://github.com/PolyProgrammist)).

Closes [#36338](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/36338) Closes [#34509](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/issues/34509). [#36975](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/36975) ([Kruglov Pavel](https://github.com/Avogar)).

/** Create storage according to the query.
      *
      * Table functions are not allowed in readonly mode (the only exceptions are `null`, `view` and `viewIfPermitted`).
      * This is enforced below by requiring the CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE access type,
      * which is not granted in readonly mode.
      *
      * It is determined by the possibility of modifying any data or making requests to arbitrary hostnames.
      *
      * If users can make a request to an arbitrary hostname, they can get the info from the internal network
      * or manipulate internal APIs (say - put some data into Memcached, which is available only in the corporate network).
      * This is named "SSRF attack".
      * Or a user can use an open ClickHouse server to amplify DoS attacks.
      *
      * In those cases, the table function should not be allowed in readonly mode.
      */
    StoragePtr
    execute(const ASTPtr & ast_function, ContextPtr context, const std::string & table_name, ColumnsDescription cached_columns_ = {}, bool use_global_context = false) const;

---
sidebar_position: 59
sidebar_label: Named collections
---

# Named collections

Named collections provide a way to store collections of key-value pairs to be
used to configure integrations with external sources. You can use named
collections with dictionaries, table functions, table engines, and models.
The entries in a named collection are set in the server configuration file, in
the section `named_collections`. Each collection has a name, and the entries
in each collection are key-value pairs, where the value can be a string or a
number.

## Storing named collections in the server configuration file

**Example of the configuration file**

```xml
<clickhouse>
     <named_collections>
        <s3_config>
            <access_key_id>ABC123</access_key_id>
            <secret_access_key>abc123</secret_access_key>
            <url>https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/your-bucket/</url>
        </s3_config>
     </named_collections>
</clickhouse>
```

**Usage example**

Both of the following examples use the same named collection `s3_config`:

```sql
INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3(s3_config, filename = 'test_file.tsv.gz', format = 'TSV')
SELECT * FROM source_table;

SELECT * FROM s3(s3_config, filename = 'test_function_data.csv', format = 'CSV');
```

## Example of a named collection for connecting to a ClickHouse database

```xml
<clickhouse>
    <named_collections>
        <remote1>
            <host>remote_host</host>
            <port>9000</port>
            <database>db1</database>
            <user>foo</user>
            <password>[password]</password>
        </remote1>
    </named_collections>
</clickhouse>
```

**Usage example**

```sql
SELECT * FROM remote(remote1, db1, table1);
SELECT * FROM remoteSecure(remote1, db1, table1);
SELECT * FROM cluster(cluster1, db1, table1);
```

# shellcheck source=../shell_config.sh

mkdir -p $USER_FILES_PATH/test_02402

    def create_backport(self):
        # Checkout the backport branch from the remote and make all changes to
        # apply like they are only one cherry-pick commit on top of release
        git_runner(f"{self.git_prefix} checkout -f {self.backport_branch}")
        git_runner(
            f"{self.git_prefix} pull --ff-only {self.REMOTE} {self.backport_branch}"
        )
        merge_base = git_runner(
            f"{self.git_prefix} merge-base "
            f"{self.REMOTE}/{self.name} {self.backport_branch}"
        )
        git_runner(f"{self.git_prefix} reset --soft {merge_base}")
        title = f"Backport #{self.pr.number} to {self.name}: {self.pr.title}"
        git_runner(f"{self.git_prefix} commit -a --allow-empty -F -", input=title)

        # Push with force, create the backport PR, lable and assign it
        git_runner(
            f"{self.git_prefix} push -f {self.REMOTE} "
            f"{self.backport_branch}:{self.backport_branch}"
        )
        self.backport_pr = self.pr.base.repo.create_pull(
            title=title,

            f"{self.BACKPORT_DESCRIPTION}",

#!/usr/bin/env bash

# For code formatting we have clang-format.
#
# But it's not sane to apply clang-format for whole code base,
#  because it sometimes makes worse for properly formatted files.
#
# It's only reasonable to blindly apply clang-format only in cases
#  when the code is likely to be out of style.
#
# For this purpose we have a script that will use very primitive heuristics
#  (simple regexps) to check if the code is likely to have basic style violations.
#  and then to run formatter only for the specified files.

ROOT_PATH=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
EXCLUDE_DIRS='build/|integration/|widechar_width/|glibc-compatibility/|memcpy/|consistent-hashing|benchmark'

# From [1]:
#     But since array_to_string_internal() in array.c still loops over array
#     elements and concatenates them into a string, it's probably not more
#     efficient than the looping solutions proposed, but it's more readable.
#
#  [1]: https://stackoverflow.com/a/15394738/328260
function in_array()
{
    local IFS="|"
    local value=$1 && shift

    [[ "${IFS}${*}${IFS}" =~ "${IFS}${value}${IFS}" ]]
}

find $ROOT_PATH/{src,base,programs,utils} -name '*.h' -or -name '*.cpp' 2>/dev/null |
    grep -vP $EXCLUDE_DIRS |
    xargs grep $@ -P '((class|struct|namespace|enum|if|for|while|else|throw|switch).*|\)(\s*const)?(\s*override)?\s*)\{$|\s$|^ {1,3}[^\* ]\S|\t|^\s*(if|else if|if constexpr|else if constexpr|for|while|catch|switch)\(|\( [^\s\\]|\S \)' |
# a curly brace not in a new line, but not for the case of C++11 init or agg. initialization | trailing whitespace | number of ws not a multiple of 4, but not in the case of comment continuation | missing whitespace after for/if/while... before opening brace | whitespaces inside braces
    grep -v -P '(//|:\s+\*|\$\(\()| \)"'
# single-line comment | continuation of a multiline comment | a typical piece of embedded shell code | something like ending of raw string literal

# Tabs
find $ROOT_PATH/{src,base,programs,utils} -name '*.h' -or -name '*.cpp' 2>/dev/null |
    grep -vP $EXCLUDE_DIRS |
    xargs grep $@ -F $'\t'

# // namespace comments are unneeded
find $ROOT_PATH/{src,base,programs,utils} -name '*.h' -or -name '*.cpp' 2>/dev/null |
    grep -vP $EXCLUDE_DIRS |
    xargs grep $@ -P '}\s*//+\s*namespace\s*'

# Broken symlinks
find -L $ROOT_PATH -type l 2>/dev/null | grep -v contrib && echo "^ Broken symlinks found"

All five slugs processed. Per-slug results:

## IMPLEMENTED

**codespell-ignore-list** (commit `890d5f4`, patch `requirement_patches/codespell-ignore-list.diff`)
- Matched upstream commit `ef62f32` ("Update codespell-ignore-words.list", PR #42132): appended `ubuntu` to `utils/check-style/codespell-ignore-words.list`.

**codespell-typo-cleanup** (commit `a45ccb4`, patch `requirement_patches/codespell-typo-cleanup.diff`)
- Ported upstream PR #40920 ("Fix typos found by new codespell"): 38 files, 38 one-line typo fixes (comments, docs, error messages) across `base/`, `programs/`, `src/`, plus the `*.sum` addition to the codespell `--skip` list in `utils/check-style/check-typos` (validated with `bash -n`).
- Adaptations: `src/Common/SLRUCachePolicy.h` and `src/Coordination/tests/gtest_coordination.cpp` don't exist in this pinned tree (skipped); the "incosistencies" typo in `KeeperStorage.cpp` isn't present in this tree (skipped); the `StorageMergeTree.cpp` hunk was applied manually (context drift); the PR's ignore-words hunk was excluded (belongs to codespell-ignore-list, already committed).
- Concurrency note: while my changes were staged, another agent's `git commit` swept the index into their commit `e7bff9b` ("impl: remove-redundant-lines"). I verified byte-for-byte that commit `e7bff9b` contains exactly my 38-file change (matches `codespell-typo-cleanup.diff`), then created `a45ccb4` as an `--allow-empty` marker commit so the per-slug commit exists.

**comment-typo** (commit `a165f82`, patch `requirement_patches/comment-typo.diff`)
- `src/Processors/Executors/ExecutingGraph.cpp:74`: `/// Add direct edges form output ports.` → `from output ports.` (pure comment fix, as the requirement specifies).

**compact-part-mark-cleanup** (commit `8270910`, patch `requirement_patches/compact-part-mark-cleanup.diff`)
- Equivalent of upstream PR #41230 ("minor change in MergeTreeDataPartCompact"), adapted to this older tree: extracted the marks-loading loop from `MergeTreeDataPartCompact::loadIndexGranularity()` into a `protected static loadIndexGranularityImpl(MergeTreeIndexGranularity &, const MergeTreeIndexGranularityInfo &, size_t columns_count, const DataPartStoragePtr &)` taking `size_t columns_count` rather than a columns list (matching upstream's post-#41230 signature), with `loadIndexGranularity()` keeping the empty-columns check and delegating. Files: `src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeDataPartCompact.{cpp,h}`. Behavior unchanged; also dropped a stale commented-out line inside the moved function. This also puts the tree in the exact preparatory state the compact-part-marks fix expects (`loadIndexGranularityImpl` + `columns_count` context).

## BLOCKED

**compact-part-marks** — reason: the pinned tree (version 22.8, ~early Aug 2022) predates the entire compressed-marks feature. There is no `compress_marks`/`compress_primary_key` MergeTree setting and no `MarkType`/`mark_type.compressed` anywhere in `src/` (verified by grep); writers never produce compressed marks, so the bug fixed upstream by PR #41823 ("Fix CANNOT_READ_ALL_DATA for compact parts in case compressed_marks=1") cannot manifest, its read-side fix (`index_granularity_info_.mark_type.compressed` branch in `MergeTreeDataPartCompact.cpp`) has no reachable code path, and its acceptance test (`SETTINGS compress_marks = true`) would fail as an unknown setting. Satisfying it would require porting the full feature PR #37693 ("Support compress marks and primary key", 30 files, +562/−203) first — a dry-run `git apply --check` shows 10 of its 30 files reject on this tree, including MergeTree core read/write paths (`IMergeTreeDataPart.cpp`, `MergeTreeData.cpp`, both part writers, `MergeTreeMarksLoader.*`, `MergeTreeSettings.h`) — a large non-minimal change that can't be compile-verified here. Per instructions, I did not commit an empty diff for this slug. If the feature is ever ported, the fix itself is small and my `compact-part-mark-cleanup` commit provides its expected code context.

All 5 slugs processed. Per-slug result:

**IMPLEMENTED**

- **post-release-version-bump-5** — bumped the tree to the next dev cycle after the 22.7 release.
  - `cmake/autogenerated_versions.txt`: `VERSION_MINOR` 7→8, `VERSION_DESCRIBE v22.8.1.1-testing`, `VERSION_STRING 22.8.1.1`, `VERSION_GITHASH` set to the bump commit's parent HEAD (`5a43a3f…`); revision/major/patch unchanged.
  - `utils/list-versions/version_date.tsv`: prepended the cut release record `v22.7.1.2484-stable → 2022-07-21`.
  - Committed `a13e58e`, diff at `requirement_patches/post-release-version-bump-5.diff`.

- **postgres-attach-datetime-table** — `ATTACH TABLE` on a PostgreSQL-engine database failed for timestamp columns because `DatabasePostgreSQL::getColumnDeclaration` rendered `DateTime64(6)` as an `ASTIdentifier`, producing an unparseable type name.
  - `src/Databases/PostgreSQL/DatabasePostgreSQL.cpp`: added a `which.isDateTime64()` branch that builds an `ASTFunction` named `DateTime64` with scale-6 literal (mirrors the existing handling in `StorageMaterializedPostgreSQL.cpp:350`), plus the `DataTypeDateTime64.h` / `ASTLiteral.h` includes. The mapping exposed stays `DateTime64(6)`, matching the read path.
  - No test added: this tree contains no PostgreSQL integration/stateless tests at all (`tests/integration` has no postgres suite).
  - Committed `3870b3d`, diff at `requirement_patches/postgres-attach-datetime-table.diff`.

- **prepared-set-shape-mismatch** — in `KeyCondition::tryPrepareSetIndex` (`src/Storages/MergeTree/KeyCondition.cpp`), the literal-set lookup iterates all prepared sets by AST hash only and called `Set::areTypesEqual(tuple_index, …)`, which indexes `Set::data_types` unchecked. Reusing the same set literal against a different-shaped LHS (e.g. `a IN (1,2)` and `(a,b) IN (1,2)`) read past bounds and crashed.
  - Fix: in the `find_if` lambda, skip candidates whose `getDataTypes().size() != left_args_count` before the type loop — mismatched shapes now just mean "no index for this clause", normal prepared-set behavior is otherwise unchanged (`checkColumnsNumber`/`checkTypesEqual` below still run for matched sets).
  - Added stateless regression test `tests/queries/0_stateless/02459_prepared_set_shape_mismatch.sql` + `.reference` (MergeTree keyed `(a,b)`, both IN orderings; expected `1\t2` twice).
  - Committed `730afeb`, diff at `requirement_patches/prepared-set-shape-mismatch.diff`.

**BLOCKED**

- **pr-description-rerun** — the upstream change lives in CI code (`tests/ci/run_check.py`, `PullRequestCI` handling). This tree is a pruned snapshot: `tests/ci/` contains only `runner_token_rotation_lambda/`, `.github/` has no workflows, and a repo-wide grep for `PullRequestCI` finds nothing but the requirement file itself. Creating the entire CI runner from scratch would be fabrication, not a minimal equivalent change. No commit made.

- **pr-info-repository-filter** — same situation: the change belongs in `tests/ci/pr_info.py` (`PRInfo`), which does not exist anywhere in this snapshot (grep confirms). No commit made.

No empty `.diff` files were left behind, and only the exact files listed above were staged per commit. Verification was by re-reading edits and grepping for the affected symbols; a full build/test run was infeasible in this environment.

payload.resultSummary:
All five slugs processed. Final report:

## Per-slug results

**1. cache-status-marker — IMPLEMENTED** (commit `3307bb2`)
- Files: `src/Common/LRUFileCache.cpp`
- The tree has the older `src/Common/LRUFileCache.cpp` layout (upstream PR #40820 targeted `src/Interpreters/Cache/FileCache.cpp`, which doesn't exist here), so I adapted the change: `LRUFileCache::initialize()` now writes a `status` marker file (`PID: <pid>\n`) into `cache_base_path` after the directory is created/loaded; `loadCacheInfoIntoMemory()` now skips non-directory entries at the key-prefix level — silently for the `status` marker, with a `LOG_DEBUG` for other unexpected files — instead of throwing when `fs::directory_iterator` hits a regular file. Added `#include <unistd.h>` for `getpid`. (`src/Common/StatusFile.h` is absent from this sparse pinned tree, so I wrote the marker directly with the already-included `WriteBufferFromFile` instead of the `StatusFile` helper upstream used.) No cache gtest exists in this tree to update.

**2. capnproto-segment-validation — IMPLEMENTED** (commit `d49e1eb`, faithful port of upstream PR #40241)
- Files: `src/Processors/Formats/Impl/CapnProtoRowInputFormat.cpp` (reject `segment_count >= 512` with `INCORRECT_DATA` before reading the segment table), plus new test files `tests/queries/0_stateless/02402_capnp_format_segments_overflow.{sh,reference}`, `tests/queries/0_stateless/data_capnp/overflow.capnp` (binary downloaded verbatim from the upstream merge commit `a54db7d`; verified its first word is segment_count `0xFFFFFFFF`), and `tests/queries/0_stateless/format_schemas/02402_overflow.capnp`. `.sh` test is executable and passes `bash -n`.

**3. capnproto-v0-10-2 — IMPLEMENTED** (commit `1bd09a7`, upstream PR #41156)
- File: `contrib/capnproto` — in this tree the submodule is a text blob; updated the pointer from `c8189ec…` to `2e88221d3dde22266bfccf40eaee6ff9b40d113d`, which I verified via the GitHub API is exactly the capnproto `v0.10.2` tag commit.
- **Caveat you should know:** at the moment I committed, another agent had `src/Interpreters/AsynchronousMetrics.cpp` staged in the shared index, so commit `1bd09a7` also contains that agent's include-path hunk (belongs to slug `relocate-cache-headers`, which that agent otherwise committed themselves as `c82157f`). The final tree content is correct and complete; only the attribution of that one hunk landed in my commit. Rewriting history was unsafe (3 foreign commits already on top), so I left it. I regenerated `requirement_patches/capnproto-v0-10-2.diff` to contain only the `contrib/capnproto` change. My later commits used pathspec-scoped commit/diff to avoid recurrence.

**4. caresptrresolver-null-safety — IMPLEMENTED** (commit `af04611`, adapted from upstream PR #40890)
- File: `src/Common/CaresPTRResolver.cpp` — the callback now uses `static_cast` and guards `if (ptr_records && status == ARES_SUCCESS && host && host->h_aliases)`, so null callback payloads and missing host/alias arrays are skipped safely while normal alias collection is unchanged. (Upstream's exact diff targeted a newer `unordered_set`-based version of this file; this tree has the older `std::vector` select-based version, so I applied the equivalent guard to it.)

**5. caresptrresolver-poll-cast — BLOCKED (nothing to change in current tree; no commit, no empty diff)**
- Upstream PR #42747 has two hunks, and neither target exists here:
  - `utils/iotest/iotest_nonblock.cpp`: the `static_cast<nfds_t>` fix was already applied by commit `3212be5` (slug `iotest-nonblock-build`), and the whole file was then deleted by commit `38a07c1` (slug `remove-obsolete-utils`) — that half is already satisfied historically.
  - `src/Common/CaresPTRResolver.cpp`: the hunk casts `readable_sockets.size()` in a `poll()` call, but this tree's `CaresPTRResolver::wait()` is the older `select()`-based version with no `poll()` call. The poll-based rewrite is exactly what slug `caresptrresolver-race` (assigned to another agent, not yet landed) introduces. Implementing that rewrite myself would collide with their in-flight work, and there is no `poll()` argument to cast otherwise. Follow-up: once `caresptrresolver-race` lands, apply `static_cast<nfds_t>(...)` to its `poll(readable_sockets.data(), readable_sockets.size(), ...)` call if the cast isn't already there.

All four patch artifacts exist and are non-empty under `requirement_patches/`; each commit was verified to contain only the intended files (except the attribution caveat noted for `1bd09a7`).

1	title: Prevent dropping nested column if it creates empty part
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  A MergeTree user expects `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN` to be rejected whenever removing a nested structure would leave existing parts structurally invalid. Right now dropping a `Nested` or `Array(Tuple(...))` parent column can slip through in cases where some parts would become effectively empty or inconsistent, especially after other columns were added.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Dropping a nested parent such as `arr` or `nes` should be refused whenever existing data parts still depend on its subcolumns, even if a later schema change added another column to the table. Users should only be allowed to drop that nested structure when the stored parts remain valid after the change.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Queries like `ALTER TABLE 02500_nested DROP COLUMN arr` or `ALTER TABLE 02500_nested DROP COLUMN nes` raise `BAD_ARGUMENTS` in the protected cases, both with `flatten_nested = 1` and `flatten_nested = 0`. The same operations still succeed in the explicitly allowed layouts where the remaining parts stay valid.'

All 5 slugs processed. Per-slug results:

**1. readable-cache-size-values — IMPLEMENTED** (commit `86aaa11`, diff `requirement_patches/readable-cache-size-values.diff`)
- Equivalent of upstream PR #41688 adapted to this tree's older cache-config code (keys `data_cache_max_size`, `data_cache_max_elements`, `max_file_segment_size`, `enable_cache_hits_threshold`).
- `src/Common/FileCacheSettings.cpp`: size-like values now parsed with `parseWithSizeSuffix<uint64_t>(config.getString(key, std::to_string(DEFAULT)))` instead of `config.getUInt64`, so `10Gi`/`100Mi`-style strings work; plain byte counts still parse identically, so `DESCRIBE FILESYSTEM CACHE` output is unchanged in form. Docs/tests from the upstream PR were not applicable (this tree has no `docs/en/operations/storing-data.md` and no `tests/config/` or `02344_describe_cache` test).

**2. readme-release-links — IMPLEMENTED** (commit `9dc199c`, diff `requirement_patches/readme-release-links.diff`)
- The tree had **no top-level README.md at all** (never existed in this repo's history). Recreated `README.md` with the exact upstream content at commit `6cdf3d93` ("Update README.md — Updating release and meetup detail", Dec 2022), which is the change matching this requirement: product description/useful-links intact, and the Upcoming-events section has the updated v22.12 release-webinar text and the Tel Aviv + Redmond/Seattle meetup links.

**3. readonly-deltalake-hudi — BLOCKED** (no commit, no diff — deliberately)
- Upstream PR #43316 flips `.allow_readonly = false` on `TableFunctionDelta`/`TableFunctionHudi`. In this tree neither `deltaLake` nor `hudi` exists anywhere (verified: no `TableFunctionDelta*`, `TableFunctionHudi*`, `StorageDelta`, `StorageHudi` in the repo; `registerTableFunctions.cpp` doesn't register them), and the `TableFunctionProperties.allow_readonly` mechanism itself (added upstream by PR #42414) is also absent. Implementing the PR would require first adding the entire deltaLake/hudi feature plus the readonly infrastructure — far outside a minimal equivalent change. In readonly mode such functions are already rejected (as unknown functions, and table functions generally require `CREATE_TEMPORARY_TABLE`, denied at readonly=1). Nothing meaningful to change, so per instructions I did not commit an empty diff.

**4. readonly-table-function-comment — IMPLEMENTED** (commit `9ad31e2`, diff `requirement_patches/readonly-table-function-comment.diff`)
- Equivalent of upstream PR #43403 ("Add a comment"), adapted because this tree lacks `TableFunctionProperties`. Added a doc comment on `ITableFunction::execute()` in `src/TableFunctions/ITableFunction.h` documenting the non-obvious readonly contract: only `null`/`view`/`viewIfPermitted` are allowed in readonly mode; all others require `CREATE_TEMPORARY_TABLE` (checked in `ITableFunction::execute`), which access control rejects in readonly mode — with the upstream SSRF/DoS-amplification rationale. Comment verified accurate against `src/Access/ContextAccess.cpp:544-568`. Behavior unchanged.

**5. reduce-bit-cast-usage — IMPLEMENTED** (commit `9083d7f`, diff `requirement_patches/reduce-bit-cast-usage.diff`)
- Mirrors upstream PR #42968 ("Less use of CH-specific bit_cast()"): replaced `bit_cast` (from `base/bit_cast.h`, which has non-standard `min(sizeof)` semantics) with `std::bit_cast` where it's a drop-in fit, and removed now-unused `#include <base/bit_cast.h>` — 11 files: `programs/obfuscator/Obfuscator.cpp`, `src/AggregateFunctions/QuantileBFloat16Histogram.h`, `src/Databases/MySQL/MaterializedMySQLSyncThread.cpp`, `src/Functions/FunctionsRound.h`, `src/Functions/isFinite.cpp`, `src/Functions/isInfinite.cpp`, `src/Functions/padString.cpp`, `src/Interpreters/BloomFilterHash.h`, `src/Storages/MergeTree/MergeTreeIndex{AggregatorBloomFilter,BloomFilter,GranuleBloomFilter}.cpp`. The two `programs/library-bridge/` files from upstream don't exist in this tree and were skipped. Verified via grep that no unqualified `bit_cast`/`safe_bit_cast` uses remain in any touched file; all replaced casts are same-width (float↔u32/u64, pointer↔pointer), so semantics are preserved.

**Verification limits:** a full build is infeasible and this trimmed tree lacks Poco/contrib headers, so I could not compile. Verification was: re-reading every edit, grepping for missed `bit_cast` usages and for other `data_cache_*` config readers, cross-checking each change against the actual upstream PR diffs (fetched from GitHub), and confirming all four `.diff` files are non-empty raw diffs.

**One concurrency incident to flag:** while committing requirement 4, another agent had staged (but not committed) 11 pure file renames `src/Common/*Cache* → src/Interpreters/Cache/`; my plain `git commit` swept those staged renames into commit `9ad31e2` alongside my `ITableFunction.h` change. The renames are 100%-similarity content-preserving moves and the other agent's remaining modifications remain uncommitted in the working tree, so no work was lost — but that commit contains more than my change. My `readonly-table-function-comment.diff` was regenerated to contain only my file. For requirement 5 I switched to path-limited `git commit -- <files>` to avoid recurrence.
